title: Factorized key-role x value-role Mirror fast memory
hypothesis: A shared key-role/value-role code bank can retrieve held-out compositional pairings with less writable state than a full pair table, while the standard Hadamard binding control tests whether the result is Mirror-specific.
physical_object: DeltaNet-style writable fast matrix state plus static role codebooks
mirror_coordinate: pair address (key-role i, value/function-role j) composing a_i elementwise-multiplied by b_j
logical_multiplicity: 36 associative mappings from 6 key roles and 6 value/function roles

selection.method: secrets.randbelow over sorted eligible P0/UNTESTED IDs after exclusions

teacher.role_code_provenance: supplied by synthetic teacher and charged; no code learning claim

development.purpose: validate serializer, delta update, held-out mask, and metrics only; no fresh tuning

paid_objects: writable DeltaNet matrix or static role codebooks

success_gate: All three fresh seeds have held-out normalized MSE <=1e-6 and factorized state uses >=10% fewer bytes than the independent full pair table; report compute and update costs separately.
mirror_specific_gate: Mirror payload <=0.90x Hadamard VSA payload at matched held-out quality.
failure_gate: Broad quality/storage gate fails, or Hadamard VSA matches Mirror quality and bytes within 10%.
boundaries: Synthetic associative recall only; not a full DeltaNet or Transformer reproduction.
Role codebooks are supplied teacher objects, not learned.
The 36 pair combinations are not independent-capacity claims.
DeltaNet fast state writes only observed pairs; held-out pairs test compositional generalization.
